bipartite.kami_theme: An address to the heavenly wind, commanding it to close up the pathway through the clouds
bipartite.shimo_theme: The wish to keep the dancing maidens (celestial dancers, or the young women performing at court) visible a little longer
bipartite.pivot_note: The kami-no-ku's command to the wind to physically close off the 'path through the clouds' is the enabling cause of the shimo's wish: by sealing the cloud-path, the wind would trap the otome (maiden dancers, imagined as celestial beings returning to the sky) on earth a little longer, allowing the speaker to keep gazing at their beautiful forms. The logic is literal and causal — block the road home, and the visitors cannot leave.

kigo.note: Clouds here are not a seasonal marker but part of the mythic conceit of the sky-path (天路) along which celestial beings travel; the poem centers on a court ritual (Gosechi dance) reference rather than a specific season, so no true kigo governs the poem despite the sky/wind/cloud imagery.

source_jp:
天つ風
雲のかよひ路
吹きとぢよ
乙女のすがた
しばしとどめむ
